rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Pre-existing (unchanged by this pin's diff), two clauses fail the rule's 2026-08-23 predicate-leak addendum ('Any clause promising what a later beat will do is cartography however the sentence starts... State the present fact; let the later module do its own work'). (1) Line 71: 'Module 4 reads this skill as part of the system you have: it walks a real task against everything you've built, and the test-strategy skill is the quality-criterion anchor in that walk.' The predicate promises what Module 4's own body will do -- the exact shape the compounded correction `2026-08-23-student_facing-later-module-predicate-is-still-cartography.md` targets, and that correction fires regardless of which section houses the sentence. (2) Line 67, trailing clause of the **What happened:** block: 'The module's close sharpens it from what the invocation showed.' This is not even rescued by an exempt section: the What-happened block already completes check_writing.md §16's 3-move shape at 'Shipped.', so this clause is a fourth, unlicensed move whose subject ('The module's close') and predicate both name a later beat's job. Checked the maintainer block for a dated accept-note authorizing either passage -- none found. Deletion test on (2): removing it and reading 'Shipped.' directly against '## What this sets up' loses nothing, since the following section already carries the Module-4 forward-pointer. Harm: cartography with a friendlier face -- it binds a beat this file doesn't own (M3's own close/debrief section, or M4's module file) to a shape it may not take, and goes stale silently if that beat's design changes without anyone re-reading this exercise file. The claim happens to be accurate to current design intent (check_student_facing.md §7 explicitly lists 'sharpen different artifact (SKILL.md...)' as canonical M2+ Debrief shape), but the rule bans the SHAPE regardless of present accuracy, precisely because today's truth doesn't protect against tomorrow's staleness.
